LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: LISTENING AND SPEAKING Theme 2: Family (Nuclear)
Topic 1.2: Listening for gist

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Listening for gist. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can one wrong pronunciation impair understanding?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify general information from given texts
2. listen to given texts for comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Listening for gist helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the differences in counting numbers above 20 in various languages,

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
